title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: Cheon d=2^20 with fixed-base windowed BSGS, a chained 2-universal matching table under a hard global 12*N link budget, 16-byte bucket heads, 128-bit node references and a 247-bit (bucket,tag) window, itemised multiword instruction derivation and a Markov success bound

claims.statement: On bls12-381-g1-ecdlp at n=2^20, with public P0 and A_i=[s^i]P0 for i=1..2^20, T=A_1=[s]P0 and s uniform in [1,r-1], the Cheon d=2^20 attack described in proof.md recovers s with success probability at least 0.85 (above the 0.39 floor) using at most 2^119.906712 total target-group-operation equivalents, W(2^20)=H+R/2000, including all preprocessing, table construction, the 2*sqrt((r-1)/2^20) fixed-base windowed scalar multiplications, hashing, matching, phase 2 and attack-side verification. Peak memory is at most 2^125 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^111.034217 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes and every runtime table is included in peak memory. The attack is classical and cold, uses no uncharged advice or quantum steps, and does not amortize work over targets. Per-operation instruction charges are DERIVED from itemised scalar AArch64 sequences under a 64-bit machine model in which addresses and indices wider than 64 bits are 2-word register quantities (proof.md P1-P4: comb lookup itemised 64, charged 200; chained hash operation itemised 203 plus 13 per extra link, whose global-budget worst case is 203+12*13 = 359, charged 560; each node is 128 bytes = 96-byte affine point + 128-bit tag + 128-bit next reference and each bucket head is a 16-byte reference, because the node arena is 2^124.43 bytes and no 64-bit field -- neither a next reference nor a bucket head -- can address it; 4-limb Montgomery chain itemised 88, charged 300; digit/loop itemised 49, charged 100). The matching table is SEPARATE CHAINING with M=2^119 buckets and the concrete 2-universal multiply-shift hash with a odd and a,b uniform per attempt; writing p=(a*x+b) mod 2^384, the bucket index is h(x)=p>>265 and the stored 128-bit tag is t(x)=(p>>137) AND (2^128-1), so (h,t) is jointly the TOP 247 BITS of p and a pair collides in both with probability at most 2/2^247. The tag is deliberately not taken from the low 128 bits: because a is odd, x=y (mod 2^128) implies t(x)=t(y) for every coin, which would destroy the 128-bit factor. no geometric probing law, no load-factor heuristic and no independence between operations is used anywhere. Work is bounded by construction, not in expectation: ONE GLOBAL COUNTER accumulates every chain link walked by the whole attempt and the attempt returns FAILURE when the counter would exceed 12*N; there is no per-operation cap and no chain is truncated, so the matching work of one attempt is at most N*203 + 12*N*13 = 359*N instructions, charged at 560*N. A SECOND GLOBAL COUNTER caps full 96-byte point comparisons at 2^20 (charged 2^20*24 = 25165824 instructions; the P2 base already contains one comparison per operation), because a tag match costs 24 instructions that the link budget does not bound. The failure probability is bounded by a first moment only: the total link count of an attempt is a sum over pairs of keys sharing a bucket, each pair colliding with probability at most 2/2^119 under 2-universality, so E[total links] <= 1.504704*N and Markov gives Pr[total links > 12*N] <= 1.504704/12 = 0.125392. That event is EXACTLY the abort event of the declared algorithm -- the global counter stops the attempt precisely when the total would exceed 12*N -- so no per-operation bound and no implication between a total and a per-operation bound is used anywhere; hence success >= 0.874608 - 2^-144 > 0.85; the comparison counter adds an independent abort term of at most 2^-143.99 by Markov, since E[false full comparisons] <= 12*N*2/2^247 = 2^-123.99. The previous revision capped each operation at 12 links and still applied Markov to the total; that implication was false and is withdrawn. No claim stronger than 0.85 is made: the earlier draft's 1-2^-100 tail is withdrawn because a first moment cannot yield such a tail and the geometric probing law it invoked does not hold for open addressing. The exponential memory is required. The bound applies at n=2^20 and any larger n because only the supplied A_d with d=2^20 is used. This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution, novelty claim or practical break.

experiments.purpose: Exercise the exact two-phase Cheon algebra, fixed-window scalar multiplication, full-point matching and d=2^k recovery on a toy prime-order group, spot-check the production digit structure on boundary and seeded scalars (the no-exception proof is analytic, not experimental), verify the factorization of r-1 and the smallest primitive root, and re-check the production parameters, the integer cost ledger and the matching cost model. This is evidence only at toy scope, never a production-cost proof. The instruction ledger of proof.md P1-P4 is itemised per operation and the ledger recomputation here checks every row, the total, the chained-table collision expectation, the Markov abort bound, the per-operation itemised charge against the 560 charge and the global 12*N link budget, and the peak-memory bound.
